title: The Continuum Model for Uniaxially Strained Bilayer Graphene Moiré Systems
authors: Tong Liu, X. R. Wang, Jiansheng Wu
abstract: We construct a continuum model for a one-dimensional moiré superlattice formed by stretching one layer of AB-stacked bilayer graphene along the x direction by a factor s. Following the spirit of the Bistritzer-MacDonald model for twisted bilayer graphene, we treat the interlayer coupling as hopping between several Dirac points. At a critical stretch factor s ~ 1.018 the two bands near the Fermi level touch, forming two degeneracy points along the k_y direction. This gap closing is accompanied by a topological phase transition, in which the Chern number changes from 1 to -1, and by a sign change of the Berry-curvature dipole, which we propose can be detected through the nonlinear Hall effect. We find that uniaxial strain modulates inter-Dirac-valley coupling, which drives band gap collapse and subsequent topological number inversion. This opens a route to engineer topological transport and quantum anomalous Hall effects via strain engineering of moiré heterostructures.
summary: This paper develops a continuum model for bilayer graphene moiré systems under uniaxial strain to study topological phase transitions. By analyzing the Hamiltonian, the authors predict that strain can induce a topological transition at a specific stretch factor (s ~ 1.018). This work opens a pathway for strain engineering to realize topological transport and quantum anomalous Hall effects.
main_problem: To construct an analytical continuum model for uniaxially strained bilayer graphene moiré systems to understand the relationship between structural strain and electronic properties, particularly topological phase transitions.
main_result: The model predicts a topological phase transition occurring at a critical stretch factor s ~ 1.018, characterized by a change in the Chern number and detectable via the nonlinear Hall effect.
method: The authors employ a continuum model approach, analogous to the Bistritzer-MacDonald model, to derive and diagonalize the effective Hamiltonian for the moiré superlattice.
model_or_system: The system is AB-stacked bilayer graphene subjected to uniaxial strain along the x-direction, forming a 1D moiré superlattice (SBLG). The Hamiltonian is constructed by treating interlayer coupling as hopping between several Dirac points.
key_observables: Chern number, band gap collapse, topological number inversion, and the nonlinear Hall effect.
important_parameters: Stretch factor (s), critical stretch factor (s ~ 1.018), and the hopping amplitudes derived from the strain.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the stretch factor s is small (s < 1.02) and makes approximations when calculating the interlayer coupling term by ignoring interactions with large in-plane separations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the structural changes due to stretching, the band structure at the critical point showing two degeneracy points along the k_y direction, and the general band structure evolution.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the continuum Hamiltonian, analyzes the low-energy physics near Dirac cones, determines the conditions for band degeneracy points, and finally links these structural changes to topological invariants like the Chern number.
why_interesting: The work provides a concrete, analytically tractable framework for engineering topological states (like QAH effects) in 2D materials using external stimuli (strain), which is highly relevant for designing quantum devices.
